log.text: Light Screen up on P1's side
Light Screen ended on P1's side

decisions.rationale: Leave Metagross (4x Fire-weak, dead vs sun) and Toxapex (passive, can't KO Kingambit). Lead Gyarados+Klefki: Rain Dance overrides Drought + Safeguard blocks Sleep Powder, shutting down the sun core. Greninja Ice Beams Venusaur (2HKO through sash). Snorlax Thick Fat tanks Fire, Brick Break 4x SE on Kingambit, Yawn/Body Slam utility.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 lost (Metagross dead weight vs sun: 4x Fire weak, 2x Ground weak). Game 2: left out Metagross+Toxapex. Brought Gyarados+Klefki+Greninja+Snorlax. Lead Gyarados+Klefki: Rain Dance (Damprock 8 turns) overrides Drought, Klefki Prankster Safeguard blocks Sleep Powder. Removes Venusaur Chlorophyll speed + Solar Beam instant charge. Greninja ExpertBelt Ice Beam 2HKOs Venusaur through FocusSash. Snorlax ThickFat resists Fire, BrickBreak 4x SE on Kingambit, Yawn alt sleep, BodySlam para. Key threats: Sableye Prankster Taunt shuts Klefki (all status moves); Raichu FakeOut disrupts setup; opponent re-establishes sun by switching Charizard out/back. If Game 3: consider Toxapex over Snorlax if opponent brings Tauros-Aqua (Snorlax 2x weak to CloseCombat). Gyarados StoneEdge 4x SE OHKOs Charizard-Y. Greninja outspeeds Charizard (189 vs 132-167) but not Venusaur under sun (200+). Kingambit SuckerPunch is win condition; bait with status moves, attack on predicted Protect/switch.

decisions.rationale: Lead Charizard/Raichu pressures likely Gyarados and Metagross leads while preserving Venusaur for sun-enabled speed and Ground pressure. Raichu deters Water attacks into Charizard and disrupts screens; Kingambit provides valuable priority into Greninja endgames.

Snorlax is the only safe switch-in vs Charizard-Y+Raichu (tanks Heat Wave 22.8-44.7% via Thick Fat, Thunderbolt 1x). Klefki is OHKO'd by Heat Wave (92.7-213.6%) and Gyarados by Thunderbolt (73.3-169.4%). Switch Klefki→Snorlax to get the tank in; Gyarados Protects to stay at 100% and waste Fake Out permanently. Plan: T2 Snorlax Yawn Raichu+Gyarados Protect, T3 switch Gyarados out (Raichu drowsy), T4 Gyarados in to Rain Dance/Stone Edge once Raichu sleeps.
decisions.notebook: Game 2 T1: Opp lead Charizard-Y+Raichu hard-counters my lead. Key damage: Raichu Thunderbolt 4x SE on Gyarados 73.3-169.4% (possible OHKO from full). Charizard-Y Heat Wave on Klefki 92.7-213.6% (possible OHKO even through Light Screen 61.6-142.4%). Gyarados Stone Edge guaranteed OHKO Charizard-Y (110.3-211.8%) but Charizard outspeeds (132-167 vs 124). Greninja Ice Beam on Charizard only 14.1-30.7% (neutral, Expert Belt irrelevant). Thunderbolt on Greninja 51.4-127.9% (possible OHKO). Snorlax safest tank: Heat Wave 22.8-44.7%, Thunderbolt 1x manageable. Plan: get Snorlax in T1, Yawn Raichu T2, preserve Gyarados for Rain Dance/Stone Edge once Raichu asleep or switched out. Opponent can switch Raichu to cure Yawn—adapt to switch-in. Klefki in back for Safeguard when Heat Wave less threatening (after Rain). Sableye Prankster Taunt shuts down Klefki and Snorlax Yawn—watch for it on predicted switches.

decisions.rationale: Mega Evolve and deny Klefki’s Prankster Light Screen with Fake Out. Sun-boosted Heat Wave has a strong chance to remove Klefki immediately while also chipping Gyarados; this prevents screens from blunting Raichu’s subsequent Thunderbolt pressure on Gyarados.
decisions.notebook: Opponent Gyarados: Jolly Damp Rock Intimidate; Protect, Stone Edge, Ice Fang, Rain Dance. It threatens Mega Charizard Y with Stone Edge and can overwrite sun. Greninja: Timid Expert Belt Protean; Protect, Hydro Pump, Ice Beam, Dark Pulse. Klefki: Bold Light Clay Prankster; Light Screen, Safeguard, Reflect, Protect—prioritize denying screens when possible. Mega Metagross: Adamant; Protect, Rock Slide, Ice Punch, Hammer Arm; Charizard-Y/Venusaur Ground pressure is valuable. Toxapex and Snorlax were omitted Game 1. Preserve Raichu’s Electric pressure for Gyarados and Kingambit priority for Greninja/Gyarados endgames; avoid Solar Beam once rain is active.

decisions.rationale: Gyarados is 4x weak to both Raichu Thunderbolt and Charizard SolarBeam, and both outspeed it—staying in is near-certain death. Switching to Klefki preserves Gyarados for later Rain Dance/Stone Edge. Klefki takes Thunderbolt (20-75%) + SolarBeam (15-49%, NVE on Steel) and likely survives if opp double-targets Gyarados's slot as expected. Snorlax Yawns Raichu, forcing switch or sleep next turn, creating safe re-entry for Gyarados.
decisions.notebook: Game 2 plan: Gyarados is primary Charizard-Y answer (Stone Edge 4x OHKO) but 4x weak to Electric/Grass and outsped by both leads. Klefki switch-in survives Thunderbolt+SolarBeam (34.7-123.5%) but dies to Thunderbolt+Heat Wave (71.3-249.2%). Yawn makes target drowsy; falls asleep end of NEXT turn; switching cures it. Opponent can switch drowsy Pokémon to cure—Yawn forces tempo not guaranteed sleep. Key damage: Heat Wave on Snorlax 13.5-40% (spread), SolarBeam on Snorlax 15.4-45.1%. Klefki Prankster screens next turn if it survives. Gyarados must wait for Raichu gone/asleep before safely using Rain Dance or Stone Edge. Watch for Sableye Prankster Taunt on predicted switches—it shuts down Klefki and Yawn. Opp back: Venusaur (Chlorophyll, SleepPowder, SolarBeam 4x on Gyarados), Kingambit (Defiant+Intimidate synergy bad for Gyarados), Tauros-Aqua (Intimidate), Sableye (Prankster Taunt/Quash/Wisp).

decisions.rationale: Double-target Gyarados: Thunderbolt plus sun-boosted Solar Beam guarantees the KO through all shown damage ranges if its reduced-success Protect fails, removing Charizard’s immediate Stone Edge/Rain Dance threat. Solar Beam acts before Gyarados, and Raichu is faster still.
decisions.notebook: Opponent Gyarados is Jolly Damp Rock Intimidate with Protect, Stone Edge, Ice Fang, Rain Dance; its repeated Protect has reduced success. Klefki is Bold Light Clay Prankster with Light Screen, Safeguard, Reflect, Protect. Snorlax is Careful Thick Fat Sitrus with Protect, Body Slam, Brick Break, Yawn. Keep Raichu’s Electric pressure for Gyarados; preserve Kingambit priority for Greninja/Gyarados endgames. Avoid relying on Solar Beam after rain is established; Charizard/Venusaur Ground pressure is valuable into Mega Metagross.

selection: Light Screen (your side, including ally Snorlax)
decisions.rationale: Klefki Prankster guarantees Light Screen before attacks—sacrificing Klefki for 8 turns of team-wide SpD support (Light Clay). Snorlax tanks any Charizard hit under screens (max 25%). Yawn on Charizard doubles sleep pressure alongside drowsy Raichu, forcing opponent to switch both or lose their weather setter to sleep. If Charizard Protects/uses non-Fire move, Klefki may survive.
decisions.notebook: Game 2 plan: Gyarados is primary Charizard-Y answer (Stone Edge 4x OHKO) but 4x weak to Electric/Grass and outsped by both leads. Klefki switch-in survives Thunderbolt+SolarBeam but dies to Thunderbolt+Heat Wave. Yawn forces tempo not guaranteed sleep—switching cures it. Light Screen via Prankster+Light Clay gives 8 turns team SpD support. Key damage WITH Light Screen+sun: Heat Wave on Klefki 65.9-110.4% (kills at 33%), Scorching Sands 28.7-49.4% (might survive), Thunderbolt on Klefki 17.1-32.3% (survives), Heat Wave on Snorlax 14.6-25.1%, Solar Beam on Snorlax 11.2-19.1%. Without screens: Heat Wave on Klefki 51.2-174.2%, Scorching Sands 34.1-115.2%, Thunderbolt 20.1-75%. Watch for Sableye Prankster Taunt on predicted switches—shuts down Klefki and Yawn. Opp back: Venusaur (Chlorophyll fast in sun, SleepPowder, SolarBeam 4x on Gyarados), Kingambit (Defiant+Intimidate synergy bad for Gyarados), Tauros-Aqua (Intimidate, AquaJet priority), Sableye (Prankster Taunt/Quash/Wisp, MentalHerb). Greninja Speed 189 outspeeds both Charizard (132-167) and Raichu (143-178) but sun weakens Hydro Pump on Charizard to effectively neutral. Next turn plan: If Klefki dies, bring Greninja (Light Screen still up). If Charizard drowsy and stays, it sleeps end of turn 4. If both foes switched, free setup turn.

decisions.rationale: Gyarados is NEUTRAL to SolarBeam (Water/Flying=2x×0.5x=1x), not 4x weak. It walls both active foes: SolarBeam 22-73%, Heat Wave 9-30% (resisted+spread), Earth Power immune. Stone Edge 4x SE on Charizard (75-259%, likely OHKO, physical so sun doesn't weaken). Rain Dance+Damprock can remove sun to nerf Venusaur Chlorophyll speed. Greninja risks OHKO from SolarBeam even through Light Screen and can't OHKO Charizard with Hydro Pump in sun. Intimidate/Defiant risk with Kingambit switch-in is manageable.
decisions.notebook: CRITICAL CORRECTION: Gyarados is NEUTRAL to SolarBeam (Water/Flying = Grass 2x × Flying 0.5x = 1x), NOT 4x weak. Gyarados walls both Charizard-Y (Heat Wave resisted 9-30% spread, Stone Edge 4x OHKO 75-259%) and Venusaur (SolarBeam neutral 22-73%, Earth Power immune via Flying). Rain Dance+Damprock removes sun, nerfing Venusaur Chlorophyll speed and Charizard fire. Greninja frail: SolarBeam 2x SE possible OHKO even through Light Screen; Hydro Pump can't OHKO Charizard in sun (water weakened). Ice Beam/Ice Fang only 2x on Venusaur (not 4x). Snorlax Yawn on Charizard forces switch or sleep. Watch Intimidate triggering Kingambit Defiant on switch-in. Sableye Prankster Taunt shuts down Rain Dance/Yawn. Game 2: down 0-1, need to win 2 straight. Light Screen 8 turns, sun 3 turns.

decisions.rationale: Switch Raichu out to deny Yawn sleep and bring fast Chlorophyll Venusaur. Scorching Sands is a guaranteed KO on 32% Klefki even through Light Screen, removing its Prankster screen/Safeguard support; it is safer than relying on spread Heat Wave damage.
decisions.notebook: Opponent Gyarados is Jolly Damp Rock Intimidate with Protect, Stone Edge, Ice Fang, Rain Dance; repeated Protect has reduced success. Klefki is Bold Light Clay Prankster with Light Screen, Safeguard, Reflect, Protect. Snorlax is Careful Thick Fat Sitrus with Protect, Body Slam, Brick Break, Yawn. Keep Raichu’s Electric pressure for Gyarados; preserve Kingambit priority for Greninja/Gyarados endgames. Avoid relying on Solar Beam after rain is established; Charizard/Venusaur Ground pressure is valuable into Mega Metagross.

selection: Rain Dance (all adjacent, including ally Snorlax)
decisions.rationale: Rain Dance removes sun (2 turns left) and sets 8-turn rain via Damp Rock, dropping Venusaur from 200-264 to 100-132 Speed and crippling Solar Beam to 2-turn/0.5x. Venusaur outspeeds Gyarados in sun but Solar Beam can't OHKO Gyarados (22-73%), so Rain Dance still goes up unless Sleep Powder hits (75% acc). Snorlax Protects to stay safe at 79% HP. Charizard is Yawned and likely switches; rain also weakens its fire moves. Next turn I can Stone Edge or Yawn Venusaur with rain active.
decisions.notebook: Gyarados neutral to SolarBeam (Water/Flying: Grass 2x × Flying 0.5x = 1x). Stone Edge 4x on Charizard-Y: 75-259%, 80% acc. Rain Dance+Damprock=8-turn rain, removes sun, drops Venusaur Chlorophyll speed to 100-132, nerfs Solar Beam to 2-turn 0.5x. Venusaur SolarBeam on Gyarados 22-73% (no OHKO from full), on Snorlax 16-49%. Charizard-Y Yawned turn 3, sleeps end of turn 4 unless switched. Watch: Raichu Thunderbolt 4x on Gyarados; Sableye Prankster Taunt shuts Rain Dance/Yawn; Kingambit Defiant triggers on Intimidate switch-in; Tauros-Paldea-Aqua Intimidate on switch-in. Greninja frail, outsped by sun Venusaur. Snorlax Thick Fat resists Fire/Ice. Series down 0-1, must win 2 straight.

decisions.rationale: Charizard must switch to avoid Yawn-induced sleep. Venusaur moves first in sun and can disable Gyarados before it threatens the incoming Raichu with Stone Edge or establishes rain; Raichu then applies immediate Electric pressure while Venusaur’s Sash covers retaliation.
decisions.notebook: Opponent Gyarados is Jolly Damp Rock Intimidate with Protect, Stone Edge, Ice Fang, Rain Dance; no revealed sleep immunity. Klefki is Bold Light Clay Prankster with Light Screen, Safeguard, Reflect, Protect. Snorlax is Careful Thick Fat Sitrus with Protect, Body Slam, Brick Break, Yawn. Preserve Raichu’s Electric pressure for Gyarados and Kingambit’s priority for Greninja/Gyarados endgames. Avoid relying on Solar Beam after rain is established; Charizard/Venusaur Ground pressure is valuable into Mega Metagross.

decisions.rationale: Gyarados is asleep and Raichu Thunderbolt can OHKO it (61.5-115.9% through Light Screen). Switching to Greninja preserves Gyarados and brings in a 189 Speed attacker that outspeeds everything post-sun. If foes targeted Gyarados, moves fail. Snorlax takes only 19-35% combined from both foes through Light Screen, so it's safe to Yawn Venusaur. Next turn sun ends: Greninja outspeeds all, Venusaur is slow+drowsy, Ice Beam breaks Sash then finish turn 7. Encore on Snorlax is manageable—Yawn resets Protect counter so forced Protects start at 100%.
decisions.notebook: Opponent roster: Charizard-Mega-Y (Drought re-sets sun on switch-in, was Yawned T3 but switched out T4 clearing it); Venusaur (Chlorophyll, Focus Sash, Modest, Sleep Powder used 1x); Raichu (LightningRod, SitrusBerry, Timid, Fake Out+Thunderbolt used); Kingambit (Defiant+LifeOrb, Adamant, 70-102 Spe); Tauros-Paldea-Aqua (Intimidate+LumBerry, Jolly, 132-167 Spe); Sableye (Prankster+MentalHerb, Careful, 70-102 Spe, has Taunt/Quash/Wisp/Recover). My team: Gyarados (Intimidate/Damprock/RainDance=8-turn rain counters Drought, currently asleep); Snorlax (ThickFat/SitrusBerry, Yawn used 2x); Greninja (Protean/ExpertBelt/189 Spe, outspeeds Raichu 143-178 and non-sun Venusaur 100-132); Klefki fainted T3. Light Screen up 6 turns. Plan: Greninja sweeps post-sun with Ice Beam for Venusaur (2x+EB, Sash saves at 1HP then finish), Hydro Pump for Raichu. Gyarados Rain Dance is key counter if Charizard-Y re-enters to re-set sun. Watch Sableye Prankster Taunt shuts Yawn/RainDance; Kingambit Defiant triggers on Intimidate.

decisions.rationale: Thunderbolt gives the best immediate chance to remove Gyarados despite Light Screen, preventing its Rain Dance and preserving Charizard’s endgame. Sleep Powder on Snorlax is higher-value disruption than minor Solar Beam chip and acts before Snorlax.
decisions.notebook: Gyarados: Jolly Damp Rock Intimidate; Protect, Stone Edge, Ice Fang, Rain Dance. Klefki: Bold Light Clay Prankster; Light Screen, Safeguard, Reflect, Protect. Snorlax: Careful Sitrus Thick Fat; Protect, Body Slam, Brick Break, Yawn. Preserve Raichu Electric pressure into Gyarados; Kingambit priority is valuable against Greninja/Gyarados. Avoid Solar Beam once rain is active; Charizard/Venusaur Ground coverage pressures Mega Metagross.

decisions.rationale: Greninja at 30% is guaranteed KO'd by Raichu Thunderbolt through Light Screen (53.6-82.8% > 30% HP). Must Protect to survive. Snorlax is asleep; if it wakes, Yawn Raichu is optimal—Raichu lacks Protect so it can't block sleep, and removing Thunderbolt threat is key to keeping Greninja alive next turn. Solar Beam charges this turn (no weather), so Venusaur isn't an immediate KO threat.
decisions.notebook: Opponent roster: Charizard-Mega-Y (Drought, Timid, was Yawned T3 switched T4 clearing it); Venusaur (Chlorophyll, FocusSash, Modest, Sleep Powder 2x used, has Protect+SolarBeam+EarthPower); Raichu (LightningRod, SitrusBerry, Timid, Fake Out used, Thunderbolt 2x used, NO Protect in moveset—vulnerable to Yawn); Kingambit (Defiant+LifeOrb, Adamant, 70-102 Spe); Tauros-Paldea-Aqua (Intimidate+LumBerry, Jolly, 132-167 Spe); Sableye (Prankster+MentalHerb, Careful, 70-102 Spe, Taunt/Quash/Wisp/Recover). My team: Gyarados (Intimidate/Damprock/RainDance=8-turn rain counters Drought, currently asleep); Snorlax (ThickFat/SitrusBerry, Yawn 2/12 used); Greninja (Protean/ExpertBelt/189 Spe, paralyzed at 30%); Klefki fainted T3. Light Screen active. Key: Raichu has no Protect so Yawn guarantees sleep unless it switches. Solar Beam needs charge turn without sun. Gyarados Rain Dance is critical counter to Charizard-Y Drought on re-entry. Watch Sableye Prankster Taunt shutting Yawn/RainDance; Kingambit Defiant triggers on Intimidate.

decisions.rationale: Thunderbolt is a guaranteed KO on Greninja from its shown HP through Light Screen if it does not Protect. Venusaur Protect covers the most likely Protect/Ice Beam line while preserving its Focus Sash and leaves both sleeping opponents under pressure next turn.
decisions.notebook: Gyarados: Jolly Damp Rock Intimidate; Protect, Stone Edge, Ice Fang, Rain Dance. Klefki: Bold Light Clay Prankster; Light Screen, Safeguard, Reflect, Protect. Snorlax: Careful Sitrus Berry Thick Fat; Protect, Body Slam, Brick Break, Yawn. Greninja: Timid Expert Belt Protean; Protect, Hydro Pump, Ice Beam, Dark Pulse. Preserve Raichu Electric pressure into Gyarados; Kingambit priority is valuable against Greninja/Gyarados. Avoid Solar Beam once rain is active; Charizard/Venusaur Ground coverage pressures Mega Metagross.

decisions.rationale: Greninja Ice Beams Venusaur for SE damage to break Focus Sash. Greninja is Normal type (Protean from last Protect), so Raichu Thunderbolt is only 0.5x with Light Screen—not guaranteed KO. If Greninja survives, Venusaur drops to 1 HP via Sash. Snorlax Protects to block Sleep Powder. Raichu falls asleep end of turn from Yawn, giving us next-turn advantage with Venusaur at 1 HP.
decisions.notebook: Opponent roster facts: Raichu has NO Protect (Fake Out/Thunderbolt/Electroweb/Encore)—Yawn guarantees sleep unless it switches. Venusaur has Focus Sash—must hit twice to KO. Charizard-Mega-Y Drought countered by Gyarados Rain Dance (8 turns w/ Damprock). Sableye Prankster can Taunt Yawn/RainDance—watch for it. Kingambit Defiant triggers on Intimidate—avoid switching Gyarados into it. Tauros-Paldea-Aqua has LumBerry—Yawn won't work. Protean type persists between turns: Greninja's current type = last move used. Snorlax Yawn is key disruption. Light Screen from Klefki (now fainted) still active. Gyarados fell asleep T4—should wake soon (1-3 turn sleep in Gen 9). Strategy: break Venusaur Sash, exploit Raichu sleep, get Gyarados in awake for Rain Dance to counter Drought on Charizard re-entry.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Thunderbolt guarantees Greninja’s KO from 30% through Light Screen if it does not Protect. Venusaur uses its immediate action to try to deny Snorlax’s Yawn/Body Slam while Raichu is about to fall asleep.
decisions.notebook: Gyarados is Jolly Damp Rock Intimidate with Protect, Stone Edge, Ice Fang, Rain Dance. Klefki was Bold Light Clay Prankster with Light Screen, Safeguard, Reflect, Protect. Snorlax is Careful Sitrus Berry Thick Fat with Protect, Body Slam, Brick Break, Yawn. Greninja is Timid Expert Belt Protean with Protect, Hydro Pump, Ice Beam, Dark Pulse. Preserve Raichu Electric pressure into Gyarados; Kingambit priority is valuable against Greninja/Gyarados. Avoid Solar Beam once rain is active; Charizard/Venusaur Ground coverage pressures Mega Metagross.

decisions.rationale: Both asleep mons may wake. If Gyarados wakes, Ice Fang (SE 2x, 23-80%) breaks Venusaur Sash; Snorlax Body Slam (21-72%) then KOs through broken Sash. If Gyarados stays asleep, Snorlax at least breaks Sash solo. Snorlax Protect is only 33% (consecutive) and makes zero progress. Venusaur Sleep Powder on Snorlax is the main risk (75%), but attacking is the only way to KO Venusaur this turn. Light Screen softens Raichu Thunderbolt (~31-104% with screen) but Gyarados may survive low rolls.
decisions.notebook: Opponent roster: Raichu NO Protect (FakeOut/TBolt/Electroweb/Encore), SitrusBerry, LightningRod. Venusaur FocusSash, Chlorophyll, Modest 100-132 Spe. Charizard-Mega-Y Drought, Timid 132-167 Spe. Kingambit LifeOrb Defiant Adamant 70-102 Spe—avoid Intimidate into it. Tauros-Paldea-Aqua LumBerry Intimidate Jolly 132-167 Spe. Sableye MentalHerb Prankster Careful 70-102 Spe—can Taunt status moves. Gyarados Rain Dance (Damprock=8 turns) counters Drought on Charizard re-entry. Snorlax Yawn key disruption but Tauros LumBerry blocks it. Venusaur must be hit twice (Sash). Light Screen 3 turns left. Down 0-1 in series, must win G2+G3. If G3: lead Klefki for screens+Safeguard vs Sleep Powder, Greninja for Venusaur pressure, Snorlax Yawn on Raichu/Charizard, Gyarados Rain Dance ASAP.

decisions.rationale: Switch Raichu to Kingambit to avoid losing a sleeping turn and retain Raichu’s decisive Electric pressure for Gyarados later. Sleep Powder targets Snorlax: its consecutive Protect is unreliable, and denying Yawn/Body Slam creates the safest board while Gyarados remains asleep.
decisions.notebook: Gyarados: Jolly Damp Rock Intimidate; Protect, Stone Edge, Ice Fang, Rain Dance. Klefki: Bold Light Clay Prankster; Light Screen, Safeguard, Reflect, Protect. Snorlax: Careful Sitrus Berry Thick Fat; Protect, Body Slam, Brick Break, Yawn. Greninja: Timid Expert Belt Protean; Protect, Hydro Pump, Ice Beam, Dark Pulse. Raichu Electric pressure is key versus Gyarados; preserve it where possible. Kingambit priority is valuable into Gyarados and Greninja. Avoid Solar Beam in rain; Charizard/Venusaur Ground coverage pressures Mega Metagross. Ice Fang from Gyarados does not OHKO full Venusaur (44.6–65%).

selection: Rain Dance (all adjacent, including ally Snorlax)
decisions.rationale: Gyarados has used 3 sleep turns (t4,7,8) and should wake now. Rain Dance is the safest play: can't be blocked by Protect or Sucker Punch (status move), sets 8-turn rain neuters Venusaur Solar Beam. Snorlax likely stays asleep but Brick Break 4x SE into Kingambit (39-82%) is best if it wakes. Snorlax survives Kowtow Cleave (41-57%). Opponent likely Protects Venusaur expecting wake-up Ice Fang—Rain Dance punishes that.
decisions.notebook: G2 T9: Gyarados 3 sleep turns used (t4,7,8)—should wake T9. Rain Dance chosen for reliability vs Protect/Sucker Punch. Damage refs: Kingambit Kowtow Cleave→Snorlax 41-57%, →Gyarados 54-77%. Venusaur EarthPower→Snorlax 11-16%. Gyarados Ice Fang→Venusaur 32-74% (Sash→1HP). Snorlax Brick Break→Kingambit 39-82% (4x SE, not guaranteed OHKO). Plan: Rain Dance now, Ice Fang Venusaur next turn to break Sash, KO turn after. Charizard on bench 100% (Yawn reset on switch-out t4). Raichu asleep on bench. Kingambit Life Orb recoil helps chip. Must win G2+G3. If G3: lead Klefki screens+Safeguard vs Sleep Powder, Greninja Venusaur pressure, Snorlax Yawn on Raichu/Charizard, Gyarados Rain Dance ASAP. Avoid Intimidate into Kingambit (Defiant). Venusaur Sash requires 2 hits. Light Screen was up (2 turns left from T9).

decisions.rationale: Switching Charizard back in restores sun before moves, making Chlorophyll Venusaur safely faster than Gyarados for Sleep Powder. This prevents an immediate Rain Dance or Ice Fang line while Charizard establishes overwhelming sun pressure next turn; Snorlax is also asleep and cannot reliably punish the switch.
decisions.notebook: Opponent sets: Gyarados is Jolly Damp Rock Intimidate with Protect, Stone Edge, Ice Fang, Rain Dance. Snorlax is Careful Sitrus Berry Thick Fat with Protect, Body Slam, Brick Break, Yawn. Klefki was Light Clay Prankster screens/Safeguard. Greninja was Timid Expert Belt Protean with Hydro Pump, Ice Beam, Dark Pulse, Protect. Metagross and Toxapex were not brought in game 2. Preserve Raichu where feasible for Gyarados; use Charizard sun to enable immediate Venusaur Solar Beams and Chlorophyll Sleep Powder. Respect rain removing Solar Beam’s instant use and Gyarados’s Stone Edge/Ice Fang. Kingambit priority remains valuable for endgames.

decisions.rationale: Stone Edge is a guaranteed OHKO on Charizard-Mega-Y (4x SE, 101-235%) if it hits (80% acc). Removing the sun setter/fire threat is critical. Rain neuters Venusaur's Solar Beam (halved) and Earth Power is immune to Gyarados. Snorlax Yawn on Venusaur punishes any non-Protect action—if it lands, Venusaur sleeps next turn, permanently ending Sleep Powder threat. Risk: Venusaur Sleep Powder on Snorlax first (75%) puts Snorlax to sleep before Yawn resolves, but Gyarados still KOs Charizard. If Venusaur targets Gyarados instead, Yawn goes off. Best EV play to swing the game.
decisions.notebook: G2 T10: Stone Edge Charizard (guaranteed OHKO if hits, 80% acc). Yawn Venusaur to disable Sleep Powder long-term. Rain Dance 7 turns left. After Charizard KO, expect Kingambit switch-in (Life Orb, Defiant—avoid Intimidate into it). Venusaur Sash still intact, needs 2 hits to KO. Gyarados Ice Fang→Venusaur 32-74%, Snorlax Body Slam→Venusaur 22-52%. Combined can KO if high rolls. Snorlax Brick Break→Kingambit 39-82% (4x SE). Kingambit Kowtow Cleave→Snorlax 41-57%, →Gyarados 54-77%. Kingambit Sucker Punch threatens Gyarados. Raichu asleep on bench. G3 plan unchanged: Klefki screens+Safeguard, Greninja pressure, Snorlax Yawn, Gyarados Rain Dance ASAP. Avoid Intimidate into Kingambit Defiant.

decisions.rationale: Protect Charizard from the immediate Stone Edge threat while Venusaur attempts to re-sleep Gyarados. This preserves the Raichu pivot for later and gives Venusaur the best chance to stop both opposing attackers before Charizard switches out and can reestablish sun on reentry.
decisions.notebook: Gyarados is Jolly Damp Rock Intimidate with Protect, Stone Edge, Ice Fang, Rain Dance. Snorlax is Careful Sitrus Berry Thick Fat with Protect, Body Slam, Brick Break, Yawn. Klefki was Light Clay Prankster screens/Safeguard; Greninja was Timid Expert Belt Protean. Metagross and Toxapex were not brought in game 2. Preserve Raichu to threaten Gyarados once awake. Mega Charizard Y can reset sun by switching out and reentering, enabling immediate Venusaur Solar Beams and Chlorophyll; Gyarados can overwrite it with Rain Dance. Kingambit is highly vulnerable to Snorlax Brick Break, so avoid exposing it while Snorlax is active unless necessary. Sleep Gyarados/Snorlax where possible, then use sun and Raichu to close.

decisions.rationale: Gyarados asleep but if it wakes, Stone Edge is guaranteed OHKO on Charizard (4x SE, 80% acc). Snorlax Protects to block Venusaur's Sleep Powder (75% acc)—the only real threat this turn. Venusaur falls asleep from Yawn EoT regardless. Charizard can't damage Gyarados (immune to Ground, 0.25x Heat Wave in rain) and does 6-27% to Snorlax. Next turn Venusaur is asleep and Gyarados gets another wake chance.
decisions.notebook: G3 plan: Klefki screens+Safeguard, Greninja pressure, Snorlax Yawn, Gyarados Rain Dance ASAP. Avoid Intimidate into Kingambit Defiant—Intimidate only triggers on Gyarados entry, not when foe switches in, so keeping Gyarados on field when Kingambit enters is safe. Opponent sets: Charizard-Mega-Y Timid CharizarditeY (HeatWave/SolarBeam/ScorchingSands/Protect); Venusaur Modest FocusSash Chlorophyll (SleepPowder/SolarBeam/EarthPower/Protect); Raichu Timid SitrusBerry LightningRod (FakeOut/TBolt/Electroweb/Encore); Kingambit Adamant LifeOrb Defiant (KowtowCleave/IronHead/SuckerPunch/Protect); Tauros-Paldea-Aqua Jolly LumBerry Intimidate (not brought G2); Sableye Careful MentalHerb Prankster (not brought G2). Key calcs: Stone Edge Gyarados→Charizard 4x SE guaranteed OHKO. Snorlax Brick Break→Kingambit 2x SE 39-82%. Kingambit KowtowCleave→Snorlax 41-57%, →Gyarados 54-77%. Sucker Punch threatens Gyarados. Rain halves Charizard Fire moves and makes Solar Beam 2-turn. Venusaur FocusSash needs 2 hits to KO.

decisions.rationale: Venusaur must switch to clear Yawn rather than become dead weight asleep. Raichu can progress its existing sleep cycle while Gyarados remains asleep and retains the key Electric endgame. Charizard’s immediate Scorching Sands is reliable chip plus burn pressure on Snorlax; Solar Beam is delayed in rain and Heat Wave is heavily dampened.
decisions.notebook: Game 2 opponent brought Gyarados, Klefki, Greninja, Snorlax; Metagross and Toxapex were absent. Gyarados: Jolly Damp Rock Intimidate, Protect/Stone Edge/Ice Fang/Rain Dance. Snorlax: Careful Sitrus Thick Fat, Protect/Body Slam/Brick Break/Yawn. Klefki: Light Clay Prankster screens/Safeguard. Greninja: Timid Expert Belt Protean, Protect/Hydro Pump/Ice Beam/Dark Pulse. Preserve Raichu as the principal Gyarados answer once awake. Charizard can reset sun by switching out and reentering, enabling immediate Venusaur Solar Beams and Chlorophyll, but Gyarados can overwrite sun with Rain Dance. Avoid exposing Kingambit to active Snorlax’s Brick Break unless necessary. Sleep opposing threats where feasible, then use sun plus Raichu to close.

decisions.rationale: Gyarados is asleep but if it wakes, Stone Edge is a guaranteed OHKO on Charizard (4x SE). Snorlax Yawn on Charizard as backup: if Gyarados stays asleep, Charizard falls asleep next turn—both foes potentially asleep in rain where Charizard is already neutered. If Gyarados wakes and KOs Charizard, Yawn is just wasted. Stone Edge miss (20%) is covered by Yawn drowsiness. Body Slam on Raichu is too unreliable (29-112%) with Sitrus Berry. Rain makes Charizard's Heat Wave negligible (5-20%).
decisions.notebook: G2 T12: Gyarados asleep but Stone Edge=guaranteed OHKO on Charizard if it wakes. Rain neutering Charizard Fire moves (Heat Wave 5-20% in rain). Raichu Thunderbolt on Gyarados 61-207% (possible OHKO). Snorlax Body Slam on Raichu 29-112% (unreliable KO, Sitrus Berry). Charizard Scorching Sands on Snorlax 9-27%. Plan: KO Charizard with Stone Edge if Gyarados wakes, Yawn as backup to sleep Charizard. If both foes asleep, free turns to attack. Down 0-1 in series, must win G2 to force G3. Remaining foes: Venusaur (FocusSash Chlorophyll, needs 2 hits), Kingambit (LifeOrb Defiant, avoid Intimidate on switch-in).

decisions.rationale: Scorching Sands provides immediate meaningful chip and a burn chance on Snorlax while avoiding rain- and Thick Fat-suppressed Fire damage. Raichu is the only clean Gyarados answer; Thunderbolt acts first if it wakes and has an OHKO roll, preventing a Stone Edge threat.

decisions.rationale: Venusaur is the safer replacement: it preserves Kingambit from Snorlax’s Brick Break and gives an immediate Sleep Powder route to disable Gyarados or Snorlax once Raichu wakes to threaten Gyarados.

Gyarados Protects to block Venusaur's Sleep Powder (spammed on Gyarados all game), Raichu's Thunderbolt if it wakes, and Kingambit's Sucker Punch if opponent switches. Snorlax Body Slams Venusaur for 22-52% chip. Next turn both awake Pokémon double-attack Venusaur for the KO through its FocusSash. Safest play that keeps Gyarados awake as main attacker while making progress.

Ice Fang 32-74%, Body Slam 22-52% on Venusaur; combined 54-126% so double attack may not always KO if Venusaur has high Def. SolarBeam only 60 BP in rain with charge turn—bad for opponent. Raichu asleep since end T7, could wake any turn; Thunderbolt 61-207% on Gyarados (possible OHKO). Kingambit Sucker Punch 35-79% on Gyarados with Life Orb. Opponent pattern: always Sleep Powders Gyarados. Plan: Protect Gyarados to block Sleep Powder/Thunderbolt/Sucker Punch, chip Venusaur with Snorlax, then double-attack for KO next turn. Down 0-1 in series, must win G2.

decisions.rationale: Put Snorlax to sleep to deny Yawn while Raichu has its earliest chance to wake and immediately threaten/possibly OHKO Gyarados with Thunderbolt. Gyarados cannot OHKO Venusaur with Ice Fang, and even a Gyarados Protect leaves Snorlax controlled for the next turn.

decisions.rationale: Raichu asleep 6 turns—likely 7-turn counter, wakes now and outspeeds Gyarados to Thunderbolt (4x SE, 61-207%, possible OHKO). Protect is only shot at blocking it. If it works, also blocks Venusaur Sleep Powder; Snorlax Body Slam chips Venusaur to ~4-34% for easy KO next turn. If Protect fails, same outcome as attacking since Raichu OHKOs first anyway. Rain Dance 3 turns left T14. Ice Fang 32-74% on Venusaur, Body Slam 22-52%; combined 54-126% so may not always KO at 56% HP. Raichu Thunderbolt 61-207% on Gyarados (4x SE, possible OHKO from 100%). Kingambit on bench at 100% with Life Orb + Sucker Punch. Opponent pattern: always Sleep Powders Gyarados. If Gyarados falls, Snorlax alone vs 2 is near-certain loss. decisions.notebook: Series lost 0-2. Opponent team patterns for reference: Charizard-Mega-Y+Venusaur+Raichu core; Venusaur spams Sleep Powder on biggest threat (Gyarados priority). Raichu LightningRod redirects Electric moves, uses Thunderbolt on Water/Flying types. Kingambit Life Orb Sucker Punch on bench as cleaner. Venusaur Focus Sash. Opponent uses weather manipulation (Charizard Sunny Day, Gyarados Rain Dance to override). Key lesson: need faster sleep counterplay (Safeguard timing, Taunt, or Safety Goggles) against Sleep Powder spam.

reflections.summary: Lost 0-2 primarily because Venusaur's Sleep Powder spam had no reliable counterplay. Klefki was brought specifically to set Safeguard but died to Scorching Sands on turn 3 before ever using it — the between-game adjustment backfired. Gyarados and Snorlax were repeatedly put to sleep, rendering two key Pokémon inactive for critical turns. Greninja was also hobbled by a Thunderbolt paralysis on turn 5. Mega Metagross was registered but left on the bench for game 2, meaning no Mega Evolution against Mega Charizard Y. The four brought (Gyarados/Klefki/Greninja/Snorlax) lacked any sleep-immune or Taunt user, and the opponent's Sun + Sleep Powder + LightningRod Raichu core exploited every weakness. Gyarados's Rain Dance override on turn 9 was too late to matter. The series was a structural mismatch against sleep spam, not a piloting error — 0 decision errors were flagged.
reflections.adjustment: In a future series against this opponent: (1) Bring Safety Goggles on a key Pokémon or include a Taunt user to shut down Sleep Powder. (2) Consider bringing Mega Metagross — its Steel typing resists Venusaur's Sludge Bomb and it can threaten with Ice Punch/Zen Headbutt; at minimum it forces different opponent positioning. (3) Mamoswine from the bench offers Ice Shard priority to pick off Venusaur before Sleep Powder connects, and Earthquake for Raichu/Charizard — strongly consider registering it. (4) If using Klefki, lead with Safeguard over Light Screen when sleep is the primary threat. (5) Reuniclus or Skeledirge from the bench could serve as sleep absorbers with recovery. (6) Do not rely on Yawn as sleep counterplay — it is too slow against Chlorophyll Venusaur under Sun.
reflections.notebook: Opponent core: Mega Charizard Y + Venusaur (Focus Sash, Chlorophyll) + Raichu (LightningRod, SitrusBerry) + Kingambit (Life Orb, Defiant) on bench. Tends to leave Tauros-Paldea-Aqua and Sableye behind. Strategy: Sun from Charizard enables Chlorophyll Venusaur speed; Venusaur spams Sleep Powder on biggest threats (priority targets: Gyarados, then Snorlax); Raichu redirects Electric moves with LightningRod and Thunderbolts Water/Flying types; Kingambit cleans late with Sucker Punch. Weather manipulation is key — opponent uses Charizard's Drought; overriding with Rain Dance is viable but must be timed before sleep lands. Venusaur Focus Sash means it survives one hit — need double-target or priority to KO through sash. Sleep Powder accuracy is 75% — opponent will accept the gamble and spam it. No reliable sleep counterplay on current roster; Safety Goggles or Taunt is mandatory for rematch. Klefki Safeguard is theoretically the answer but Klefki is too fragile to guarantee it lands — consider a bulkier screener or leading Safeguard immediately. Snorlax Yawn is insufficient as reciprocal sleep because Venusaur outspeeds under Sun. Key prep conclusion: register Mamoswine (Ice Shard priority vs Venusaur) and/or a Taunt user; bring Mega Metagross to contest the Mega slot.

reflections.summary: Won game 2 and the series 2-0 because the Charizard-Y/Raichu lead immediately pressured the Gyarados/Klefki/Snorlax structure, removed Klefki before screens could become decisive, and Venusaur's Sleep Powder repeatedly denied both Gyarados and Snorlax. Raichu then preserved the endgame by eliminating Greninja and Gyarados. The between-game approach helped: Venusaur's sleep disruption and retaining Raichu for Gyarados were central. The four brought—Charizard-Y, Venusaur, Raichu, Kingambit—fit well; Mega Charizard Y was the appropriate evolution for immediate sun pressure and a strong Venusaur partner, though it remained exposed to Gyarados's revealed Stone Edge after rain replaced sun. Kingambit was largely unused, so it was not essential to this specific game, but was a reasonable reserve into Klefki/Metagross possibilities. Series preparation was broadly strong: the registered six covered rain, screens, and bulky balance, while Dragonite, Altaria, Emolga, and Avalugg had no demonstrated reason to displace the selected core. The main vulnerability was relying on imperfect-accuracy Sleep Powder and allowing Gyarados rain plus Stone Edge to trade Charizard; it did not alter the result because Raichu and Venusaur retained control.
reflections.adjustment: For a future series, keep the Charizard-Y/Venusaur/Raichu core as the primary anti-Gyarados plan, but treat Charizard as expendable only after it has secured key pressure and avoid leaving it exposed once Gyarados is awake under rain. Preserve Raichu's awake turns for direct Gyarados pressure; use Fake Out, Encore, or Protect-aware targeting to exploit Snorlax and Gyarados's repeated Protects rather than depending exclusively on Sleep Powder. Continue bringing Kingambit if Mega Metagross is likely, but consider Tauros-Aqua as an alternative fourth if a more direct rain-resistant physical pivot is needed. Preparation should retain the six registered; no left-behind Pokémon has shown a clearer matchup role than the current group.
reflections.notebook: Opponent's demonstrated game-2 structure was Gyarados/Klefki/Greninja/Snorlax; Mega Metagross and Toxapex were omitted. Gyarados: Jolly Intimidate, Damp Rock, Protect, Stone Edge, Ice Fang, Rain Dance; it can overwrite sun and threatens Mega Charizard Y with Stone Edge. Klefki: Light Clay Prankster screens with Safeguard and Protect; remove or pressure it early before screen support compounds bulk. Greninja: Timid Expert Belt Protean with Protect, Hydro Pump, Ice Beam, Dark Pulse; Raichu Thunderbolt threatens it heavily. Snorlax: Careful Thick Fat Sitrus with Protect, Body Slam, Brick Break, Yawn; it uses Yawn repeatedly and can remove screens, but is vulnerable to disruption and sleep. Charizard-Y plus Venusaur gives immediate sun/chlorophyll pressure, while Raichu is the crucial Gyarados answer and should be kept healthy and awake when possible. Sleep Powder was highly effective at denying their bulky double-Protect/Yawn/rain game, but misses and sleep turns should not be assumed. Watch for repeated Protect probabilities and use Encore when it offers a safe punish.
